extracted.intended_audience: government communications professionals (GCS) and national security communicators
extracted.subtask_description: A government (GCS) delivery model for national security communications describing five pillars (ABCDE) to guide planning and execution of strategic communications in the national security context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building alliances
rubrics_metrics.description: identifying influential stakeholders; communicating mutual interests; shaping the debate by telling the story; capitalising on UK’s soft power advantage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus outreach on influential stakeholders, articulate shared interests, craft narratives that shape public/policy debate, and leverage the UK’s soft power to strengthen partnerships and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: identifying a theory of change; using behavioral science (COM-B, EAST); effecting change by influencing audiences; analysing impact in real time and long run
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design interventions grounded in an explicit theory of change; apply behavioural frameworks such as COM-B and EAST to target capability/opportunity/motivation; measure and analyse effects in real time and over the long term to iterate activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing context
rubrics_metrics.description: scanning for trends, risks & opportunities; providing situational awareness; influencing the information environment; exposing disinformation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously monitor trends and risks to provide decision-makers with situational awareness; proactively frame issues to influence the information environment and identify/expose disinformation where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplifying deterrence
rubrics_metrics.description: explaining HMG’s objectives; building resilience in domestic audiences; projecting UK capability; demonstrating cost of malign action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should clearly articulate government objectives, strengthen domestic audience resilience, visibly project capability where appropriate, and demonstrate consequences/costs of hostile or malign actions to deter adversaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional expertise and capability
rubrics_metrics.description: convening the XWH community to provide full spectrum of communications skills; building capability alongside allies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring together cross‑whitehall (XWH) communications expertise to deliver a full range of skills and invest in capability-building with partners and allies to ensure sustained, coordinated delivery.
